status: FINAL. This is the closing status artifact for the Model 1 (LSTM autoencoder anomaly detector) work in this repository.

scoring_rule.name: S2 -- final-timestep MSE
scoring_rule.formula: mean((x[:, -1, :] - reconstruction[:, -1, :])^2) over the 55 reconstructed features at the window's final timestep only

threshold_selection: selected using validation data only (percentile-grid-of-pre-fault-validation-scores procedure, see configs/model1/protocol_config.json threshold_selection_rule) -- never recalculated on test
process_statement: The held-out test set was evaluated only after architecture, preprocessing, scoring rule, and threshold were frozen (experiments/model1/final_model_selection.json); no post-test tuning was performed. Held-out test evaluation was performed exactly ONCE. No retraining, re-scoring, threshold recalibration, or second test evaluation occurred at any point, including after seeing this result.
final_outcome: Held-out success criteria were NOT met. All three locked targets (F1 >= 0.82, median detection delay <= 10s, pre-fault FPR <= 0.05) passed on validation and failed on test. Candidate B + S2 remains the frozen final Model 1 configuration per instruction; no further architecture, scoring-rule, or threshold change was made in response to this result.
failure_study_findings: Held-out known-normal reconstruction-score distributions shifted relative to validation, especially for CPU and MEM test cases.
The CPU/MEM false-positive (pre-fault FPR) increase on held-out data was concentrated in a small subset of cases, not spread uniformly across all CPU/MEM cases.
LOSS-fault held-out post-injection sensitivity was substantially weaker than on validation.
Within the tested architecture range (22,727-242,263 parameters), capacity changes did not materially improve the validation detection-delay result.
see_also: experiments/model1/failure_study/ for descriptive (non-model-changing) analysis of the validation-to-test generalization gap.
